newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal tuna firm seeks partner for boat purchases.
newsitem.headline: Senegal tuna firm seeks partner for boat purchases.

text.p: Senegal's main fish canner, Societe Nouvelles des Conserveries du Senegal (SNCDS), is seeking investors in new tuna boats to help it overcome fish supply uncertainty, a company spokesman said on Friday.

"We are looking for partners...sometimes its difficult to find tunny-fish (tuna) in the market," Finance Director Ahmadou Yeri Diop told Reuters, pointing to shortage of international supply but rising processing capacity at SNCDS.
"Up to recently we had avoided investing in boats but now its part of our priorities," he added.
SNCDS spends 10 billion CFA a year on tuna supplies from Ivory Coast, Spain, Seychelles and Thailand and aims to process 20,000 tonnes of fish in 1997, he said.
"We have increased our production capacity, which can be up to 25,000 tonnes," Diop said. "We are also aiming at having partners for a fish flour factory," he added.
SNCDS, 65 percent Senegalese-owned, sends 99.9 percent of its exports to Europe - mainly France, England, Germany, Italy, Denmark, Spain and Tunisia.
Turnover totalled 14.2 billion CFA in 1996 against 13.6 billion in 1995 and about 3.5 billion had been invested between 1993 and 1996, said Ahmadou.

SNCDS is 35 percent-owned by France's Groupement de Pecheurs de France. Senegal recently renewed a fishing agreement which gives 148 European Union fishing vessels access to Senegalese fishing grounds.
